explanation: For each neighboring word pair, add the first differing character's ordering edge; reject a longer word before its own prefix. Topologically sort all seen characters and reject cycles.
timeComplexity: O(W+S+E+V squared log(V+1)) general upper bound: adjacent comparisons and graph construction are linear in input, but each of V removals sorts the current ready array again; shift can also move O(V) entries. Under the fixed lowercase alphabet V≤26.
spaceComplexity: O(S + V + E) auxiliary space, including concatenated input characters. The graph stores V vertices and E distinct edges; this implementation also concatenates input characters.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 JavaScript algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: The first differing characters in adjacent sorted words give a necessary alphabet precedence edge; later characters cannot affect that comparison. A longer word before its own prefix is impossible. Any topological ordering of all seen characters satisfies every extracted comparison, while a cycle proves no alphabet can satisfy them all.
walkthrough: Words ["ca","cb","da","db"] require a before b and c before d. One valid character order is "abcd"; using it keeps all four words sorted. The algorithm’s smallest-ready-character rule returns that order.
edgeCases: Every seen character appears once, even if it has no ordering edges.
A longer word preceding its own prefix returns an empty string.
Several different alphabet orders may be valid.
